title: Interim Role Handover and Accountability Protocol
author: Marta Chen
content:
Purpose

This document defines a standardized protocol for interim role handovers and short-term accountability when a role is vacated temporarily or permanently and a direct hire/replacement is not yet in place. The protocol balances continuity of critical work with clear ownership, performance expectations, and timeboxed escalation. It is intended for people-ops, hiring managers, and engineering/product managers responsible for operational continuity.

Scope

- Applies to individual contributor and manager roles across engineering, product, go-to-market, and support functions for interim periods up to 180 days.
- Not intended for executive succession (SVP/VP) or legal-mandated transitions — contact People Ops and Legal for those scenarios.

Definitions

- Interim Owner: The person (or small team) assigned formal ownership for the role's core responsibilities during the interim window.
- Handover Window: Scheduled overlap time for knowledge transfer (if available).
- Coverage Plan: Documented list of responsibilities matched to interim owners and SLAs.
- Role Gate: A checkpoint at 30/90/180 days to decide hiring, extension, or deprecation.

Principles

1. Timebox: Interims are explicitly time-limited with a Role Gate decision at 30/90/180 days.
2. Single Source of Truth: All coverage plans, decision logs, and performance notes are stored in the role's Confluence page and restricted to the role's stakeholders.
3. Minimal Disruption: Preserve customer-facing SLAs and platform reliability.
4. Transparent Expectations: Interim owners receive written scope, deliverables, and performance criteria.

Quick summary (one-line)

When someone leaves or is out for an extended period, assign an Interim Owner, publish a Coverage Plan within 48 hours, run a 30/90/180 Role Gate cadence, and escalate to People Ops for hiring triggers or policy exceptions.

Owner Responsibilities

- People Ops: coordinate formal assignment, maintain hiring timeline, schedule Role Gates, update compensation/hiring approval trackers.
- Manager (vacating role manager or next-level manager): define priority responsibilities, approve Coverage Plan, and conduct interim compensation approvals if required.
- Interim Owner: accept written scope, log weekly status, and participate in Role Gate reviews.

Pre-handover checklist (to publish within 48 hours)

- Role summary (one paragraph): core responsibilities, recurring events, stakeholders.
- Active projects and status (top 5).
- Weekly recurring commitments and required capacity (hours/week).
- Critical credentials and access owners (no secrets in doc; reference vault locations).
- Known risks with mitigation steps.
- Stakeholder contact list and escalation path.

Step-by-step Protocol

1) T+0 to T+48 hours: Immediate stabilization
   - People Ops coordinates assignment of Interim Owner(s).
   - Manager publishes Coverage Plan draft to Confluence and marks page as "Interim - <role>".
   - Notify stakeholders via standard template (see templates section).

2) T+3 to T+7 days: Detailed handover
   - Knowledge transfer sessions scheduled (30–60 minutes) for critical systems, documented in the Coverage Plan.
   - Interim Owner confirms access and runbook familiarity.
   - Manager and Interim Owner agree on measurable deliverables for the first 30 days.

3) Weekly status cadence
   - Interim Owner posts a 1–2 sentence weekly update in the Coverage Plan page.
   - Manager and People Ops review updates; if coverage is insufficient, escalation begins (see Escalation).

4) Role Gates (decision cadence)
   - 30-day Gate: Confirm hiring timeline + stopgap adjustments. Decision options: continue interim, open req, or deprecate role scope.
   - 90-day Gate: Assess long-lead hiring progress; if candidate pipeline insufficient, approve extension or redistribute responsibilities.
   - 180-day Gate: Final decision — either full-time hire offer or permanent redistribution. If exceptions needed, escalate to Head of People and Finance.

Templates (communication and acceptance)

- Interim assignment notification (email):
  Subject: Interim coverage for <Role> — <Interim Owner Name>

  Body: "Hello team — Per today's update, <Interim Owner> will serve as interim owner for <Role> through the next Role Gate on <date>. Coverage Plan: <link>. Immediate questions to <Manager Name>. People Ops will run regular check-ins and keep the hiring timeline updated."

- Interim owner acceptance (Slack):
  "I accept interim ownership for <Role> beginning <date>. I have access to the runbooks and will publish weekly updates to the Coverage Plan."

Performance & feedback during the interim period

- Expectations are timebound. Interim Owners receive focused feedback aligned to the temporary scope; this feedback does not substitute for performance reviews tied to a permanent role.
- Managers must document any skill gaps, concerns, or exemplary behaviors in the Coverage Plan as evidence for future hiring or role design decisions.

Compensation and crediting

- Compensation adjustments for interim ownership (e.g., acting pay) require manager justification and People Ops approval.
- Crediting: work done in interim is credited to the interim owner for promotion and performance evidence, but role-level promotions require an established permanent role or new job posting.

Decision matrix (text table)

| Trigger | Action Owner | Timeline | Outcome options |
|--------|-------------|----------|----------------|
| Unplanned vacancy | Manager + People Ops | 48 hours | Assign interim, publish Coverage Plan |
| Insufficient coverage | Manager | 7 days | Add additional interim resource or escalate to Director |
| Hiring runway >90d | People Ops | 30 days | Approve interim extension / open req / redistribute |
| Critical incidents | SRE/Manager | immediate | Emergency escalation, all-hands runbook |

Escalation path

1. Manager -> Director of the team (for resource/budget changes)
2. Director -> Head of People (for role design or policy exceptions)
3. Head of People -> CFO/Legal (for compensation, headcount, or compliance questions)

Temporary delegation patterns (recommended)

- Pattern A — Full interim owner: single person accepts all responsibilities and is empowered to make day-to-day decisions. Best for small, low-risk roles.
- Pattern B — Split ownership: responsibilities divided across two owners (operations vs product). Use for roles with distinct execution and stakeholder responsibilities.
- Pattern C — Backup rotation: three-person rotation covering on-call and recurring tasks. Use when the work requires full-time continuity but hiring is delayed.

Monitoring metrics and SLAs

- Coverage Plan must track 3 metrics during interim:
  - Operational SLA adherence (e.g., incident MTTR, uptime %)
  - Project milestone completion rate for top 3 projects
  - Stakeholder satisfaction (qualitative note weekly)

Example scenario (illustrative)

- Situation: Senior ML Engineer leaves unexpectedly.
  1. Within 24 hours, manager assigns an interim owner (senior peer).
  2. Coverage Plan lists top priorities: model serving stability, two active rollouts, code review backlog.
  3. Interim owner agrees to 8 hours/week for code reviews and leads on-call.
  4. 30-day Gate: hiring manager approves open req; pipeline slow -> 90-day extension approved.
  5. At 180 days, final hire made and ownership transitioned with documented lessons learned.

- Secondary reviewers: Manager community (quarterly review).
